evidence.fit: The sample runs in-page with 'Nothing here is uploaded or sent.' evidence.distinctiveness: The page uses the product's own grammar on itself: superscript citations in the copy, a 'Notes on this page' section ('Every claim above carries a note or a flag, the way an answer should'), and FLAGGED chips on the company's own missing metrics. The handoff table and the 'Not for you yet if your policies live in people's heads' line are specific to this product. Less distinctive: system Helvetica/Liberation sans with mono labels is a common docs-SaaS look, and the four-step numbered list is conventional.
evidence.proof: At 1440 the full finished artifact sits beside the headline in the first viewport: question, a five-line agent log ('Searched your policy library: 14 documents, 212 sections. Nothing else.'), a cited draft with [1]/[2], and two source cards quoting the policy text with section and review date. The second tab 'Q 9.1 Penetration test FLAGGED' shows the other half: 'No source in your policies, so nothing was drafted' with the closest passage named and rejected. Both outcomes of the core promise are shown and labelled 'Illustrative'. Weaker than A on sentence-level checking: the citation markers are not linked to highlighted spans.
evidence.craft: Tokenised type scale (h1 clamp to 44px, 17px body, 13px mono labels), consistent rules and greys, clear hierarchy, and axe reports 0 violations at 390 and 1440. Defects: footnote superscripts render at 8.84–11.5px (smallest_text_px 8.84) with 10×11px hit areas; during 'Replay the draft' at 1440 the card holds its min-height while the lower half is empty white for ~2s; at 320 the header breaks into three rows and the nav labels wrap ('How it / works'). evidence.mobile: 390: recomposed rather than shrunk. Nav becomes a second header row of 44px links, the hero CTA goes full width (52px), the sample tabs stack vertically as 48px full-width rows with the chip right-aligned, and the reviewer actions become two equal full-width buttons; status changes appear in place directly above where you tapped. No overflow. Against it: the card starts around y≈770 so the artifact is on the second screen, the footnote links are tiny tap targets, and the page is very long.
evidence.honesty: Sample labelled in the card header, at the point of use ('Illustrative: a made-up questionnaire and made-up policies'), and the reviewer is tagged '(sample)'. The CTA states what it does before you commit ('Opens a blank email…'). Missing metrics, unnamed partners and lack of pricing are stated as flagged facts without sounding apologetic. evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390: tabs switch by click and Arrow keys (roving tabindex); 'Replay the draft' re-reveals the log lines and then the draft, sources and review, and disables itself while running; Approve / Send back / Write the answer / Mark not applicable each change a role=status line with specific outcome text ('Returned to drafting with her note… it cannot add anything the library does not say'), hide the actions and move focus to a 'Reset the sample' button that restores them. evidence.copy: Concrete, consistent vocabulary (cited / flagged / approve / send back) used identically in copy, chips and the demo. Good microcopy: 'Nothing to upload, no call to book', 'We will not print a number we have not measured', 'a thin library produces a thin draft and a long flag list'. Some repetition: the four-step 'How it works', the handoff table and the two role columns restate the same flow three times.
evidence.first_screen: 1440×900: specific promise, named approver, CTA with stated behaviour and the live labelled artifact showing a cited answer with its sources, all without scrolling. 390×844: headline, lede, full-width CTA and its explanation are in view, but only the card's title row ('Sample questionnaire · Northwind Logistics') is visible at the fold, so the phone viewport has the promise without the proof.

problems: On the phone the artifact starts at the fold and the page runs to about 8,000px, with the flow explained three times (steps, handoff table, role columns).
Footnote superscripts are 8.84–11.5px with roughly 10×11px tap targets, yet the page leans on them as its trust device.

Citation markers and blue source names in the agent log look interactive but do nothing, and the cited answer is not tied to highlighted passages at the sentence level, so the 'checked' half is shown less vividly than the 'drafted' half.

reason: B puts the whole promise, a labelled working sample showing both a cited and a flagged answer, and an honestly described email action into the first 1440 viewport, and gives each audience a real path through the handoff and role sections. A has the more vivid sentence-to-passage check and lovely copy, but its proof sits below the fold, its 'Your call' step approves itself with a dead Send back, and it slips in an unsupported 'one pass instead of three' claim. A version of A with the demo in the first screen, a reviewer step the visitor actually operates, and that claim removed would make this close.
